output.brief: The proximity-bias diagnosis is not supported by the data we have. The dashboard gap mostly reflects eligibility: 32% of remote staff have 18+ months in level versus 74% of office staff. Once eligible, remote and office employees were nominated at nearly the same rate (28% each) and approved at similar rates (20% vs 21%). That difference is within chance with 110 remote people. Remote staff also have a higher share of recent hires, which is the more likely driver. I'm fairly but not fully sure: the stretch-assignment question and attrition are not yet tested, and the staffing data cannot show who got high-visibility work. Recommend: do not announce the three-day office rule. It would exclude about 180 home-based remote staff on a diagnosis the data does not support. Instead, re-run promotion reporting comparing only eligible remote and office staff, check whether hiring timing explains the gap, and set up a visible process for stretch assignments. Re-check at the FY2027 cycle.
